s: India's separation from Madagascar began 88 million years ago, after the breakup of Gondwana. For the latest Cretaceous and most of the Paleocene it was an isolated landmass, known as Insular India.
k: About 88 million years ago India began to break away from Madagascar. For a long time after that it was a giant island.

s: The Deccan Traps of west-central India are one of the largest volcanic features on Earth. Their eruptions lasted 600,000 to 800,000 years, between about 66.3 and 65.6 million years ago, and left basalt more than 2 kilometres thick over about 500,000 square kilometres.
k: About 66 million years ago lava poured out over western India for hundreds of thousands of years. It left a layer of black rock two kilometres thick.

s: The Indian plate moved north at about 20 cm a year and is believed to have begun colliding with Asia as early as 55 million years ago. The Himalayas are the result of that collision, which is still going on.
k: About 55 million years ago India began to push into Asia. The ground crumpled up and became the Himalaya.

s: Sivapithecus is a genus of extinct apes. Fossil remains now assigned to it, the oldest dated to 12.2 million years ago in the Miocene, have been found since the 19th century in the Sivalik Hills of the Indian subcontinent and in Kutch.
k: Twelve million years ago apes called Sivapithecus lived in South Asia. Their fossils have been found in the Sivalik Hills.

t: Before and after the Toba eruption
s: At Jwalapuram in Andhra Pradesh, stone tools lie both under and over layers of volcanic ash left by the Toba eruption of about 74,000 BC, showing habitation before and after the event.
k: About 76,000 years ago a giant volcano called Toba erupted, and its ash fell on India. At Jwalapuram, stone tools lie both below the ash and above it.

s: Lonar Lake in Maharashtra is a salty soda lake in a crater made by a meteorite impact. Earlier analyses dated it to about 52,000 years ago. A later method gave a much older age of 570,000 years, which is disputed.
k: Lonar Lake fills a hole made when a rock from space hit the Earth. Scientists do not agree on when: perhaps 52,000 years ago, perhaps much earlier.

s: The Bhimbetka rock shelters in central India span the Paleolithic and Mesolithic periods and show the earliest traces of human life in India. The earliest of their cave paintings are dated to 10,000 BCE.
k: In rock shelters at Bhimbetka, people painted pictures on the walls about 12,000 years ago.

s: Lahuradewa, in the Upper Gangetic Plain of Uttar Pradesh, is noted to have been occupied as early as 9,000 BCE. It provides the oldest evidence of ceramics in the Indian subcontinent.
k: At Lahuradewa in the Ganges plain, archaeologists found the oldest pottery known in the Indian subcontinent.

s: Mehrgarh, on the Kacchi Plain of Balochistan near the Bolan Pass, is a Neolithic and Chalcolithic site where a small farming village began around 7000 BCE.
k: Mehrgarh is one of the oldest farming villages in South Asia. People there grew wheat and kept animals about 9,000 years ago.

s: Inside the Edakkal caves, in the Wayanad district of Kerala, are petroglyphs believed to date to at least 6,000 BCE, from the Neolithic period.
k: In caves high in the hills of Kerala, people carved pictures into the rock at least 8,000 years ago.

s: Amri is an ancient settlement in today's Sindh, south of Mohenjo-daro, that goes back to 3600 BCE.
k: Amri in Sindh is an old village site that goes back about 5,600 years.

s: Kot Diji, about 45 km south of Khairpur in Sindh, is an ancient site of the Indus Valley Civilisation, estimated to have been occupied around 3300 BCE.
k: Kot Diji was a town of the early Indus people, lived in about 5,300 years ago.

s: The Burzahom site in the Kashmir Valley has revealed four phases of culture between 3000 BCE and 1000 BCE. Evidence of wheat was found there.
k: At Burzahom in Kashmir, early farmers lived from about 5,000 years ago. They grew wheat.

s: The Ahar or Banas culture was a Chalcolithic culture of south-eastern Rajasthan, lasting from about 3000 to 1500 BCE, contemporary with and adjacent to the Indus Valley civilisation. Balathal is one of its ninety known sites.
k: While the Indus cities flourished, farming villages that used copper grew up next door in Rajasthan.

s: Harappa was a settlement in the Punjab, near a former course of the Ravi River. It gave its name to the Harappan, or Indus Valley, civilisation, whose mature phase lasted from 2600 to 1900 BCE.
k: Harappa was one of the great cities of the Indus people. The whole civilisation is often called Harappan after it.

s: Ganweriwala, in the Cholistan Desert of southern Punjab, was one of the largest cities of the Indus Valley civilisation.
k: Ganweriwala was one of the biggest Indus cities. Today its ruins lie in a desert.

s: Sutkagan Dor, on the Makran coast near Gwadar, close to the Iranian border, is the westernmost known site of the Indus Valley civilisation.
k: The Indus people built towns far from their rivers. The westernmost one known is on the coast near Iran.

s: Chirand, on the northern bank of the Ganga in Bihar, has a large prehistoric mound with Neolithic, Chalcolithic and Iron Age settlements stacked in layers, dating from 2500 BC. Evidence of wheat was found.
k: At Chirand beside the Ganga, people lived in the same spot for thousands of years. Each village was built on top of the last.

s: Lothal, in the Bhal region of Gujarat, was one of the southernmost sites of the Indus Valley Civilisation. Construction is believed to have begun around 2300 BCE.
k: Lothal was a town of the Indus people in what is now Gujarat. It is more than 4,000 years old.

t: An Indus trading colony on the Oxus
s: Shortugai, in northern Afghanistan, was a trading colony of the Indus Valley Civilisation, established around 2000 BC on the Oxus river near the lapis lazuli mines.
k: The Indus people set up a trading post far away in northern Afghanistan, near the mines of a blue stone called lapis lazuli.

s: The Ochre Coloured Pottery culture is a Bronze Age culture of the Indo-Gangetic Plain, generally dated 2000–1500 BCE, extending from eastern Punjab to north-eastern Rajasthan and western Uttar Pradesh.
k: About 4,000 years ago villagers of the upper Ganges plain made a kind of pottery that archaeologists can recognise by its ochre colour.

s: Sinauli, an archaeological site in western Uttar Pradesh between the Ganga and Yamuna, gained attention for its Bronze Age vehicles with solid disk wheels, found in 2018.
k: In 2018 archaeologists at Sinauli dug up Bronze Age vehicles with solid disk wheels.

s: The Cemetery H culture was a Bronze Age culture of the northern subcontinent, in today's Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, from about 1900 BCE until about 1300 BCE.
k: After the great Indus cities declined, a new culture took their place in the Punjab.

s: The Kuru kingdom, a union of the Bharata and Puru tribes in northern India, appeared in the Middle Vedic period, about 1200 to 900 BCE.
k: The Kuru kingdom was one of the first kingdoms of northern India, in the time when the Vedas were being composed.

s: Magadha was a region and kingdom based in the eastern Ganges Plain. It was one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas of the second period of city-building.
k: Magadha was a kingdom beside the river Ganges. Later, great empires grew out of it.

s: The Painted Grey Ware culture is an Iron Age culture of the western Gangetic plain and the Ghaggar-Hakra valley, conventionally dated from about 1200 to 600–500 BCE.
k: In the early Iron Age the villages of the upper Ganges plain made fine grey pots with painted patterns.

s: Gandhara was an Iron Age kingdom of north-western South Asia. Its people were called the Gandharis.
k: Gandhara was an old kingdom in the north-west of South Asia.

s: Anga was an ancient Indo-Aryan tribe of eastern South Asia whose existence is attested during the Iron Age.
k: Anga was an ancient people and kingdom in the east of India.

s: Kashi was an ancient kingdom of India whose existence is attested during the Iron Age.
k: Kashi was a very old kingdom of India.

s: Taxila, historically Takshashila, in today's Punjab province of Pakistan, was founded around 1000 BC and is one of the oldest cities in Asia. It is a World Heritage Site.
k: Taxila, in today's Pakistan, is one of the oldest cities in Asia. It was founded about 3,000 years ago.

s: Adichanallur, in the Thoothukudi district of Tamil Nadu, has been the site of very important archaeological finds. Carbon dating of samples excavated in 2004 showed they belonged to the period between 1000 BC and 600 BC.
k: At Adichanallur in Tamil Nadu, archaeologists found things buried between 3,000 and 2,600 years ago.

s: Hire Benakal in Karnataka is a megalithic site, among the few in India that can be dated: to the period from 800 BCE to 200 BCE.
k: At Hire Benakal in Karnataka there are megaliths, monuments built of great stones, more than 2,000 years old.

s: Kosala was one of the Mahajanapadas of ancient India. It emerged as a small state during the Late Vedic period.
k: Kosala was one of the sixteen big states of ancient northern India.

s: Avanti was a Mahajanapada roughly corresponding to today's Malwa region. Buddhist texts list it among the sixteen great states.
k: Avanti was a kingdom in central India, in the region now called Malwa.

s: The Vajjika League, also called simply Vajji, was an ancient Indo-Aryan tribal league or confederacy.
k: The Vajji were a league of clans who joined together.

s: Surasena was an ancient region corresponding to today's Braj in Uttar Pradesh, with Mathura as its capital.
k: Surasena was an old kingdom whose capital was the city of Mathura.

s: Vatsa, or Vamsa, was one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas named in the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya.
k: Vatsa was one of the sixteen great states of ancient India.

s: Matsya was an ancient Indo-Aryan tribe of central India, attested during the Iron Age, who were organised into a kingdom.
k: The Matsya people had one of the old kingdoms of India.

s: The Mallas were an ancient tribe of north-eastern South Asia whose existence is attested in the Iron Age.
k: The Mallas were one of the peoples of ancient north India who are known from very old texts.

s: The Ashtadhyayi is a grammar text that describes a form of the Sanskrit language. It is attributed to Panini, and its composition is dated to somewhere between the 6th and 4th centuries BCE.
k: About 2,500 years ago a scholar named Panini wrote down the rules of the Sanskrit language in a famous book.

s: Keeladi is a settlement site of the Sangam period under excavation. A specialist on the dig dated the excavated remains to between the 6th and the 3rd century BCE.
k: At Keeladi in Tamil Nadu, archaeologists are digging up a town from the time of the old Tamil poems.

s: In a war of about 540 to 535 BCE, the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha defeated the neighbouring Anga kingdom.
k: Long ago the kingdom of Magadha fought its neighbour Anga and won. Magadha was starting to grow.

s: Pataliputra, beside today's Patna, was first built by the Magadha ruler Ajatashatru in 490 BCE as a small fort near the Ganges.
k: The great city of Pataliputra began as a small fort by the river Ganges in 490 BCE. Today the city of Patna stands next to it.

s: In the Magadha–Vajji war, the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha fought the neighbouring Vajjika League, which was led by the Licchavis.
k: The kingdom of Magadha went to war with the Vajji league of clans next door.

s: Chandraketugarh, a cluster of villages in the Ganges Delta about 35 km north-east of Kolkata, is an archaeological site of ancient Bengal.
k: Chandraketugarh is a place in Bengal where archaeologists have found the remains of a very old town.

s: The Kingdom of Anuradhapura, named for its capital city, was the second established Sinhalese kingdom of ancient Sri Lanka.
k: Anuradhapura was the capital of a great kingdom in ancient Sri Lanka.

s: The Nanda Empire governed Magadha and the Gangetic plains in the 4th century BCE, with an enormous reach across north-eastern India.
k: Before the Mauryas, the Nanda kings ruled a huge empire along the river Ganges.

t: Indian campaign of Alexander the Great
s: Alexander the Great's Indian campaign lasted from 327 to 325 BC. After conquering the Persian Empire, the Macedonian army marched into the north-west of the subcontinent.
k: Alexander the Great, a king from far-away Macedon, led his army into north-western India for two years.
src: Indian campaign of Alexander the Great

s: At the Battle of the Hydaspes in May 326 BC, the Macedonian army of Alexander the Great fought the Pauravas under King Porus on the river now called the Jhelum.
k: In 326 BC Alexander the Great fought King Porus beside the Jhelum river.

s: Boukephala and Nikaia were two cities founded by Alexander the Great on either side of the Hydaspes, today's Jhelum River, during his invasion.
k: Alexander founded two new towns on the banks of the Jhelum river after his battle there.

s: From November 326 to February 325 BC Alexander the Great campaigned against the Mallians of the Punjab while marching down-river.
k: On his way home, Alexander fought the Mallian people of the Punjab.

s: The Maurya Empire, with its power base in Magadha, was founded by Chandragupta Maurya around 320 BCE and lasted until 185 BCE.
k: Chandragupta Maurya founded the first empire to rule most of India, more than 2,300 years ago.

s: Between 305 and 303 BCE Seleucus I Nicator, ruler of the Seleucid Empire, crossed the Indus and confronted the Maurya Empire.
k: Seleucus, ruler of the Seleucid Empire, crossed the river Indus and met the army of the Mauryas.

s: The Tirukkural, or Kural, is a classic Tamil text on everyday morality made of 1,330 short couplets of seven words each. It has been dated variously from 300 BCE to the 5th century CE.
k: The Kural is a famous Tamil book of 1,330 tiny two-line poems about how to live a good life.

s: The Chola dynasty was a Tamil dynasty of southern India. At its height it ruled an expansive maritime empire.
k: The Cholas were a family of Tamil kings in the far south of India. Much later they built a great empire of the sea.

s: The Pandyas of Madurai were an ancient Tamil dynasty, one of the three great kingdoms of the Tamil country alongside the Cholas and the Cheras.
k: The Pandya kings ruled from the city of Madurai. They were one of three great Tamil royal families.

s: Chandragupta Maurya is said to have died on the hill of Chandragiri at Shravanabelagola in 298 BCE, after becoming a Jain monk and taking up an ascetic life.
k: A Jain tradition says that the emperor Chandragupta Maurya gave up his throne, became a monk and died at Shravanabelagola in the south.

s: The pillars of Ashoka are a series of monolithic columns dispersed throughout the subcontinent, erected, or at least inscribed with edicts, by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka, who reigned from 268 to 232 BC.
k: The emperor Ashoka set up tall stone pillars across India, each cut from a single piece of rock, and had his messages carved on them.

s: The Kalinga War, which ended about 261 BCE, was fought between the Mauryan Empire under Ashoka and Kalinga, an independent kingdom on the east coast.
k: The emperor Ashoka fought a war against Kalinga, a kingdom on the east coast of India.

s: The Ajanta Caves are 30 rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments in Maharashtra, made between the second century BCE and about 480 CE. They are a World Heritage Site.
k: At Ajanta, Buddhist halls were cut into a cliff and painted with beautiful pictures. The work went on for more than 600 years.

s: The Grand Trunk Road is one of the oldest and longest major roads in Asia, running about 3,655 km from Bangladesh to Kabul. It was built in the 3rd century BCE along an ancient route called the Uttarapatha.
k: The Grand Trunk Road is one of the oldest and longest roads in Asia. People have travelled along its route for more than 2,000 years.

s: The Barabar Hill Caves in Bihar are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India. They date from the Maurya Empire, and some carry inscriptions of Ashoka, in the name of "King Piyadasi".
k: The oldest rooms carved out of solid rock in India are at Barabar in Bihar. They were made in the time of the emperor Ashoka.

s: The Great Stupa at Sanchi, on a hilltop in Madhya Pradesh, was originally commissioned by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. It is one of the oldest stone structures in India.
k: The emperor Ashoka had a great stone dome, called a stupa, built at Sanchi more than 2,200 years ago.

s: The Lion Capital of Ashoka is the head of a column erected by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka at Sarnath about 250 BCE. It is crowned by four life-sized lions set back to back.
k: About 250 BCE the emperor Ashoka set up a pillar at Sarnath with four stone lions on top. Today the lions are the emblem of India.

s: The Amaravati Stupa, now ruined, stands at the village of Amaravathi in Andhra Pradesh. It was probably built in phases between the third century BCE and about 250 CE.
k: A great Buddhist stupa was built at Amaravati in Andhra Pradesh over about 500 years. Today it is a ruin.

s: The Major Rock Edicts of the emperor Ashoka are 14 detailed edicts, among the earliest dated rock inscriptions of any Indian monarch. Ashoka, who ruled from 268 to 232 BCE, called his inscriptions Dhamma Lipi, inscriptions of the Dharma.
k: The emperor Ashoka had fourteen long messages to his people carved on great rocks, more than 2,200 years ago. The pin marks Brahmagiri in Karnataka, one of the places where edicts of his were found.

s: The Satavahanas, called the Andhras in the Puranas, were an ancient Indian dynasty of the Deccan.
k: The Satavahana kings ruled the Deccan, the high land in the middle of India.

s: The Natya Shastra is a Sanskrit treatise on the performing arts, attributed to the sage Bharata. Its first complete compilation is dated to between 200 BCE and 200 CE, though estimates vary.
k: The Natya Shastra is a very old Sanskrit book that explains how to act, dance and make music.

s: The Shunga Empire, centred on Magadha, controlled most of the northern subcontinent from around 187 to 75 BCE. It was established by Pushyamitra, who took the throne from the Mauryas.
k: A man named Pushyamitra took the throne of Magadha from the Mauryas and started the Shunga line of kings.

s: The Battle of Vijithapura was a decisive battle in the campaign of the Sri Lankan king Dutthagamani against the South Indian king Elara.
k: In Sri Lanka, King Dutthagamani fought King Elara, who had come from southern India.

s: The Tolkappiyam is the oldest extant Tamil grammar and the oldest extant long work of Tamil literature. It is difficult to date: one scholar places its earliest layer between the 2nd and 1st century BCE, another dates it no earlier than the 2nd century CE.
k: The Tolkappiyam is the oldest book of Tamil grammar that still exists. Nobody is sure how old it is: its first parts may be about 2,000 years old.

t: Buddhist caves of the Western Ghats
s: The Bhaja Caves near Pune are a group of 22 rock-cut caves dating back to the 2nd century BC. The nearby Karla Caves were developed from the 2nd century BCE to the 5th century CE.
k: More than 2,000 years ago Buddhist monks had prayer halls cut into the cliffs of the hills near Pune.

s: The Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves near Bhubaneswar include finely carved caves made in the 2nd or 1st century BCE. In one of them, the Hathigumpha, is a Jain inscription of seventeen lines in Prakrit, written in Brahmi script.
k: Near Bhubaneswar are caves carved for Jain monks more than 2,000 years ago. One has a long message cut into the rock in a very old script.

s: Bharhut, in the Satna district of Madhya Pradesh, is known for a Buddhist stupa whose carved panels are each labelled in Brahmi characters. Recent authors date the reliefs of its railings to about 125–100 BCE.
k: At Bharhut the carvings on a Buddhist stupa have labels in writing that tell you what each picture shows. They are about 2,100 years old.

s: The Charaka Samhita is a Sanskrit text on Ayurveda, setting out theories of physiology, diagnosis and anatomy. Revised by Charaka between 100 BCE and 200 CE, it is considered one of the most authoritative texts of Indian medicine.
k: The Charaka Samhita is a very old Indian book about medicine and keeping healthy. It was written about 2,000 years ago.

s: The Indo-Parthian kingdom, known as the Pahlavas in Sanskrit texts, was founded by Gondophares I in the first century CE.
k: A king named Gondophares founded a kingdom in the north-west that mixed Persian and Indian ways.

s: The Kushan Empire, about 30 to 375 CE, was formed by the Yuezhi. First based in Bactria, it spread across much of today's Afghanistan, Pakistan and northern India.
k: The Kushans built an empire that stretched from Afghanistan deep into India.

s: The Western Satraps, or Western Kshatrapas, were Indo-Scythian (Saka) rulers of the western and central parts of India.
k: The Western Satraps were Saka kings who ruled western and central India.

s: Trade between the Indian subcontinent and the Roman Empire took the southern sea route by the Red Sea from around the beginning of the first century AD. Arikamedu, near Pondicherry, is an archaeological site of this period, excavated in the 1940s.
k: About 2,000 years ago ships sailed between India and the Roman Empire. Near Pondicherry, archaeologists have dug up an old port from that time.

s: Muslin, a fine cotton fabric of plain weave, was hand woven in Bengal and exported for many centuries. Muslin from the region is mentioned in the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, written around 2,000 years ago.
k: Weavers in Bengal made muslin, a very fine cotton cloth. Traders were already carrying it abroad 2,000 years ago.

s: The Arthashastra is an ancient Sanskrit treatise on statecraft, politics, economic policy and military strategy. It is likely the work of several authors over centuries, compiled into a new treatise in the 1st century CE.
k: The Arthashastra is an ancient Indian book about how to run a kingdom: its money, its army and its laws.

s: The Saint Thomas Christians, also called Syrian Christians of India, are a community of Indian Christians who trace their origins to the evangelistic activity of Thomas the Apostle in the 1st century.
k: Christians have lived in Kerala for a very long time. Their tradition says that Thomas, a follower of Jesus, came to India in the first century.

s: Takht-i-Bahi, at Mardan in today's Pakistan, is the site of an ancient Buddhist monastery, founded in the 1st century CE and in use until the 7th century.
k: Takht-i-Bahi is an old Buddhist monastery in the hills of Pakistan. Monks lived there for 600 years.

s: The Kanheri Caves are rock-cut monuments in a basalt outcrop on the island of Salsette, in today's Sanjay Gandhi National Park. They hold Buddhist sculptures, paintings and inscriptions dating from the 1st to the 10th century CE.
k: In the forest on the edge of Mumbai are caves that Buddhist monks carved and used for about 900 years.

t: The Kallanai dam on the Kaveri
s: Kallanai is an ancient dam across the Kaveri river in Thanjavur district, 15 km from Tiruchirappalli, built by Karikala of the Chola dynasty in 150 CE.
k: Almost 1,900 years ago a Chola king named Karikala built a stone dam across the Kaveri river.

s: The Vakataka dynasty originated in the Deccan in the mid-3rd century CE.
k: The Vakataka kings ruled in the Deccan from about 1,750 years ago.

s: The Kalabhras ruled all or parts of the Tamil region some time between the 3rd and 6th centuries.
k: The Kalabhras ruled the Tamil country some time between 1,700 and 1,400 years ago.

s: The Pallava dynasty ruled in southern India from 275 to 897, over a significant part of the Deccan and the region of Tondaimandalam.
k: The Pallava kings ruled part of southern India for more than 600 years.

s: The Venkateswara Swami Temple, also known as the Tirumala or Tirupati Balaji Temple, is a Hindu temple in the hills of Tirumala.
k: The Tirumala temple is a famous Hindu temple in the hills.

s: The Gupta Empire existed from the mid 3rd to the mid 6th century CE and at its peak spanned much of the northern subcontinent.
k: The Gupta kings ruled much of northern India. Many people remember their time as a golden age.

s: Changu Narayan is a Hindu temple on a hilltop in Bhaktapur District, Nepal, built in the 4th century.
k: Changu Narayan is a very old Hindu temple on a hill in Nepal.

s: The Kadambas were an ancient royal family of Karnataka who ruled northern Karnataka and the Konkan from Banavasi.
k: The Kadamba kings ruled part of Karnataka from their capital, Banavasi.

s: The Gauda kingdom arose in the Gauda region of Bengal, in today's West Bengal and Bangladesh.
k: Gauda was an early kingdom of Bengal.

s: Abhijnanashakuntalam, The Recognition of Shakuntala, is a Sanskrit play by the poet Kalidasa. Its exact date is uncertain, but Kalidasa is often placed in the 4th century CE.
k: The poet Kalidasa wrote a famous play in Sanskrit about a girl named Shakuntala. He probably lived more than 1,600 years ago.

s: Kamarupa, also called Pragjyotisha, was an early state of the Classical period and, along with Davaka, the first historical kingdom of Assam.
k: Kamarupa was the first kingdom we know of in Assam, in India's north-east.

s: Nalanda was a renowned Buddhist monastery and centre of learning in Magadha, in today's Bihar. It operated for almost a thousand years, from 427 CE until around 1400 CE.
k: Nalanda was a great Buddhist place of learning in Bihar. Students lived and studied there for almost a thousand years.

s: The iron pillar of Delhi, 7.21 metres high and 41 cm across, was made in the time of Chandragupta II.
k: In Delhi stands an iron pillar more than seven metres tall. It was made in the time of the Gupta king Chandragupta II.

s: The Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh, in the Betwa River valley of Uttar Pradesh, is a Hindu temple of the early 6th century.
k: The Hindu temple at Deogarh was built about 1,500 years ago.

s: The Halmidi inscription, found in a village of the Hassan district of Karnataka, is the oldest known inscription in the Kannada language. It is often dated to between 450 and 500 CE.
k: A stone found at the village of Halmidi carries the oldest writing we know in the Kannada language. It is about 1,500 years old.

s: The Cilappatikaram, a poem of 5,730 lines, is the earliest Tamil epic. It tells a tragic love story of ordinary people, is attributed to the prince turned Jain monk Ilango Adigal, and was probably composed in the 5th century CE.
k: The Cilappatikaram is the oldest long story-poem in Tamil. It is a sad love story about ordinary people, not kings.

s: The Maitraka dynasty ruled the Kingdom of Valabhi in western India from about 475 to 776, from their capital at Vallabhi.
k: The Maitraka kings ruled Gujarat for 300 years from the city of Vallabhi.

s: The Maukharis were a post-Gupta dynasty who controlled the plains of the Ganga and Yamuna from Kannauj for almost a century.
k: After the Guptas, the Maukhari kings ruled the Ganges plain from the city of Kannauj.

s: The Aryabhatiya, a Sanskrit astronomical treatise, is the only known surviving work of the 5th-century mathematician Aryabhata. The historian Roger Billard estimates it was composed around 510 CE.
k: Around the year 510 the mathematician Aryabhata wrote a famous book in Sanskrit about the stars and planets.

s: At the Battle of Sondani in 528 CE, a confederation of Indian rulers led by King Yashodharman fought the Alchon Hun king Mihirakula.
k: In 528 Indian kings joined forces under King Yashodharman to fight the Hun king Mihirakula.

s: The Chalukya dynasty ruled large parts of southern and central India between the 6th and the 12th centuries.
k: The Chalukya kings ruled the Deccan for hundreds of years.

s: The Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, is a Hindu temple dedicated to Vishnu, and one of the 108 Divya Desams.
k: This famous temple of the god Vishnu stands in the city of Thiruvananthapuram in Kerala.

s: The Maligawila Buddha statue in Sri Lanka is a standing figure of the Buddha carved out of a large limestone rock in the 7th century.
k: In Sri Lanka there is a tall standing Buddha carved from a single great rock about 1,400 years ago.

s: Nataraja is a depiction of Shiva as the divine cosmic dancer. Stone reliefs at the Ellora Caves and the Badami Caves, made by around the 6th century, are among the oldest Nataraja sculptures in India.
k: Nataraja is the god Shiva shown as a dancer. Some of the oldest carvings of him, about 1,500 years old, are in the caves at Badami.

s: The Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya in Bihar marks the place where the Buddha is said to have attained enlightenment. What is visible today dates from the 6th century CE, or possibly earlier, with several major restorations.
k: A tall temple at Bodh Gaya marks the spot where the Buddha is said to have understood the truth. Most of it is about 1,500 years old.

s: The Elephanta Caves, on an island in Mumbai's harbour, are a collection of cave temples mainly dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva. They are most commonly placed between the 5th and 7th centuries, and many scholars consider them complete by about 550 CE.
k: On an island near Mumbai are cave temples with giant carvings of the god Shiva.

s: Chamba State, founded in the late 6th century, was one of the oldest princely states in what is now India.
k: Chamba, in the Himalaya, was one of the oldest of India's princely states.

s: The Ellora Caves in Maharashtra are one of the largest rock-cut cave complexes in the world, with Hindu, Buddhist and Jain artwork dating from AD 600 to 1000.
k: At Ellora there are Hindu, Buddhist and Jain cave temples, carved between the years 600 and 1000.

s: The Karkota dynasty, about 625 to 855 CE, ruled the Kashmir valley and some northern parts of the subcontinent.
k: The Karkota kings ruled Kashmir for more than 200 years.

s: The Battle of Makran in 644 CE was fought between the Rashidun Caliphate and the Chach dynasty of Sindh.
k: In 644 an Arab army fought the king of Sindh.

s: The Battle of Ghaghra, fought in 1529, was a major battle in the conquest of India by the Mughal Empire.
k: In 1529 the Mughals fought another big battle, at Ghaghra.

s: The Madurai Nayaks were a Telugu-speaking dynasty who ruled large parts of today's Tamil Nadu between the 16th and 18th centuries, with Madurai as their capital. The line was founded around 1529 as a viceroyalty under the Vijayanagara Empire.
k: From about 1529 the Nayak rulers governed much of the Tamil country from the city of Madurai.

s: In 1531 a combined Ottoman and Gujarati force defeated a Portuguese attempt to capture the city of Diu.
k: In 1531 the Portuguese tried to capture the port of Diu and were beaten off.

s: The Thanjavur Nayak dynasty was established by Sevappa Nayaka around 1532 and governed Thanjavur.
k: The Nayak rulers governed the old Chola city of Thanjavur from about 1532.

s: Bengaluru, also known as Bangalore, is the capital and largest city of Karnataka. Its founding is dated to 1537.
k: The city of Bengaluru was founded in 1537.

s: In the siege of Diu in 1538, an army of the Sultanate of Gujarat, aided by forces of the Ottoman Empire, attempted to capture the city from the Portuguese.
k: In 1538 the Sultan of Gujarat and his Ottoman allies tried to take Diu from the Portuguese.

s: The Battle of Chausa in 1539 was a notable engagement between the Mughal emperor Humayun and the Afghan ruler Sher Shah Suri.
k: In 1539 the emperor Humayun fought Sher Shah Suri at Chausa.

s: The Sur Empire, founded by Sher Shah Suri, was ruled by the Afghan-origin Sur dynasty in northern India between about 1540 and 1556, with Sasaram as its capital. It held nearly all the former Mughal lands of the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
k: Sher Shah Suri took northern India away from the Mughals and ruled it from 1540. His family lost it again in 1556.

s: Hunza, also known as Kanjut, was a Burusho kingdom in the present-day Gilgit-Baltistan region.
k: Hunza was a small kingdom high in the mountains of the far north.

s: Banke Bihari Temple is a Hindu temple in the town of Vrindavan, in the Mathura district of Uttar Pradesh.
k: The Banke Bihari Temple is a Hindu temple in the town of Vrindavan.

s: Chaturbhuj Temple at Orchha in Madhya Pradesh is a Hindu temple dedicated to Vishnu.
k: The Chaturbhuj Temple at Orchha is a temple of the god Vishnu.

s: Jag Mandir is a palace built on an island in Lake Pichola. It is also called the Lake Garden Palace.
k: Jag Mandir is a palace on an island in Lake Pichola.

s: Machilipatnam, also known as Masulipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh was an ancient port town where European traders settled from the 16th century. It was a major trading port for the Portuguese, British, Dutch and French.
k: Masulipatnam was a busy port on India's east coast. From the 1500s traders from Portugal, Holland, Britain and France all came there.

s: The Ramcharitmanas is an epic poem in the Awadhi language, composed by the 16th-century bhakti poet Tulsidas. Its chief inspiration is the Ramayana of Valmiki.
k: In the 1500s the poet Tulsidas retold the story of Rama in a long poem in the Awadhi language.

t: The langar, a kitchen for everyone
s: In Sikhism a langar is the community kitchen of a gurdwara, which serves meals free of charge to all, regardless of religion, caste, gender, wealth or ethnicity. It was started by the Sikh Gurus.
k: Every Sikh gurdwara has a kitchen called a langar where anyone at all can eat for free. The Sikh Gurus began the custom.

s: The Akbari Sarai is a large caravan inn in Shahdara Bagh in Lahore.
k: The Akbari Sarai in Lahore was a big inn where travelling merchants and their animals could rest.

s: The Battle of Sirhind was fought between the Mughal Empire and the Sur Empire in 1555.
k: In 1555 the Mughals fought the Sur rulers at Sirhind.

s: The Second Battle of Panipat was fought on 5 November 1556 between the Mughals under Akbar and King Hemu.
k: In 1556 the young emperor Akbar's army fought King Hemu at Panipat.

s: The tomb of the Mughal emperor Humayun in Delhi was commissioned in 1558 by his first wife and chief consort, Empress Bega Begum, who personally chose its Persian architects.
k: The tomb of the emperor Humayun in Delhi was ordered by his wife, the empress Bega Begum, in 1558.

s: The Sé Cathedral of Santa Catarina in Goa is the cathedral of the Latin Church Archdiocese of Goa and Daman.
k: The Se Cathedral is the main church of the Catholic archdiocese of Goa. It stands in Old Goa and is part of a World Heritage Site.

s: Adham Khan's Tomb is the 16th-century tomb of Adham Khan, a general of the Mughal emperor Akbar.
k: The tomb of Adham Khan, one of the emperor Akbar's generals, was built in the 1560s.

s: The Hamzanama tells the legendary exploits of Hamza, an uncle of Muhammad. Its best-known copy is the enormous illustrated manuscript commissioned by the Mughal emperor Akbar about 1562.
k: Around 1562 the emperor Akbar ordered a giant illustrated book of adventure stories.

s: Tansen, born at Gwalior, was a Hindustani classical musician. In 1562, at about the age of 60, he joined the court of the emperor Akbar, where his performances were recorded by many court historians.
k: Tansen, born at Gwalior, was a great musician. In 1562 he went to sing at the court of the emperor Akbar.

s: Rani Durgavati was regent queen of the Gond kingdom of Gondwana from 1550 to 1564, during the infancy of her son. She is mainly remembered for her battles against the Mughal invasion. She died on 24 June 1564.
k: Rani Durgavati ruled the Gond kingdom for her young son. She fought the Mughal army that invaded her land, and died in 1564.

s: The Battle of Talikota in 1565 was a watershed battle between the Vijayanagara Empire and an alliance of the Deccan sultanates. The defeat of Aliya Rama Raya led to the eventual collapse of Vijayanagara.
k: In 1565 the Deccan sultans joined forces and defeated the Vijayanagara Empire at Talikota. The empire never recovered.

s: Agra Fort, also known as the Red Fort of Agra or Qila-i-Akbari, is a historic fort in the city of Agra.
k: Agra Fort is a great red fort that the Mughal emperors lived in.

s: In 1567–1568 the Mughal Empire under Akbar besieged Chittorgarh in an expedition against the Kingdom of Mewar.
k: The emperor Akbar's army surrounded the great fort of Chittorgarh in 1567.

s: The Paradesi Synagogue, or Mattancherry Synagogue, stands in Jew Town in Kochi, Kerala. It dates from 1568.
k: There is a synagogue in Kochi that was built in 1568. Jewish people have lived in Kerala for a very long time.

s: Fatehpur Sikri, about 36 km from Agra, was founded as the capital of the Mughal Empire in 1571 by Emperor Akbar. It served as capital until 1585 and was completely abandoned in 1610.
k: The emperor Akbar built a whole new capital city at Fatehpur Sikri in 1571. He left it only fourteen years later.

s: The Sidi Saiyyed Mosque in Ahmedabad, popularly known as Sidi Saiyyed ni Jali, was built by Sidi Sayyad, a Habshi nobleman.
k: A famous mosque in Ahmedabad was built by Sidi Sayyad, a nobleman whose family came from Africa.

s: The Battle of Tukaroi in 1575 was fought between the Mughal Empire and the Bengal Sultanate.
k: In 1575 the Mughals fought the Sultan of Bengal at Tukaroi.

s: The battle of Haldighati was fought on 18 June 1576 between the Mewar forces led by Maharana Pratap and the Mughal forces.
k: In 1576 Maharana Pratap of Mewar fought the Mughal army at Haldighati.

s: The Jama Masjid of Bijapur, in Karnataka, is a congregational mosque dating from 1576.
k: The great Friday mosque of Bijapur was built in 1576.

s: The Battle of Rajmahal in 1576 took place between the Mughal Empire and the Karrani dynasty that ruled the Sultanate of Bengal.
k: In 1576 the Mughal army fought the sultans of Bengal at Rajmahal.

s: The pool on the site of the Golden Temple at Amritsar was completed by the fourth Sikh Guru, Guru Ram Das, in 1577. The temple is the pre-eminent spiritual site of Sikhism.
k: In 1577 the fourth Sikh Guru finished a great pool at Amritsar.

t: Chand Bibi, regent of two sultanates
s: Sultana Chand Bibi was regent of the Bijapur Sultanate during the minority of Ibrahim Adil Shah II, from 1580 to 1590, and later regent of the Ahmednagar Sultanate.
k: Chand Bibi ruled the kingdom of Bijapur for ten years while its sultan was a child. Later she ruled Ahmednagar too.

s: Din-i Ilahi was a short-lived syncretic theology propounded by the Mughal emperor Akbar in 1582.
k: In 1582 the emperor Akbar put forward a set of beliefs of his own that mixed ideas from several religions. It did not last long.

s: Galle Fort, on the south-west coast of Sri Lanka, was first built by the Portuguese in 1588 and later extended.
k: The Portuguese built a fort at Galle in Sri Lanka in 1588.

s: The Ain-i-Akbari, the "Administration of Akbar", is a detailed account of how the Mughal Empire was run under the emperor Akbar. His court historian Abu'l Fazl wrote it in Persian between 1589 and 1596.
k: The emperor Akbar's historian wrote a book describing exactly how the Mughal Empire was run.

s: The Golden Temple in Amritsar, Punjab, is a gurdwara and the pre-eminent spiritual site of Sikhism.
k: The Golden Temple in Amritsar is the holiest place of the Sikh religion.

s: Junagarh Fort stands in the city of Bikaner, Rajasthan. It was originally called Chintamani.
k: Junagarh Fort is the great fort of the city of Bikaner.

s: The Charminar, constructed in 1591, is a monument in Hyderabad, Telangana, and a symbol of the city.
k: The Charminar, a building with four tall towers, was built in Hyderabad in 1591.

s: Amer Fort, or Amber Fort, stands in the town of Amer in Rajasthan.
k: Amber Fort is a palace-fort on a hill near Jaipur.

s: Kumbhalgarh, a fortress in the Aravalli Hills of Rajasthan built in the 15th century by Rana Kumbha, is known as the Great Wall of India: its wall runs for 36 kilometres.
k: Kumbhalgarh fort has a wall 36 kilometres long. People call it the Great Wall of India.

s: Gagron Fort, in the Jhalawar district of Rajasthan, is a hill and water fort.
k: Gagron Fort in Rajasthan is both a hill fort and a water fort.

s: Sri Dalada Maligawa, the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic, is a Buddhist temple in Kandy, Sri Lanka.
k: In Kandy there is a famous temple that holds a tooth said to be the Buddha's.

s: The Synod of Diamper was a Catholic synod held at Udayamperoor in June 1599 that made rules and regulations for the ancient Saint Thomas Christians of the Malabar Coast.
k: In 1599 a church meeting in Kerala made new rules for the old Christian community there.

s: The Qissa-i Sanjan, the Story of Sanjan, is a Persian verse narrative written by the Parsi priest Bahman Kaikobad in 1599. It tells how Zoroastrian refugees fled Iran after the Arab conquest and settled in India.
k: In 1599 a Parsi priest wrote down the story of how his people's ancestors fled from Iran long ago and found a new home in India.

s: Thanjavur painting is a classical South Indian painting style from the town of Thanjavur in Tamil Nadu. It goes back to about 1600, when the Nayakas of Thanjavur encouraged the arts.
k: Around the year 1600 painters in the town of Thanjavur began a rich style of painting that is still made today.

s: Akbar's tomb, the mausoleum of the third Mughal emperor, was built in 1605–1613 by his son Jahangir.
k: The emperor Akbar is buried in a grand tomb built by his son Jahangir.

s: The Guru Granth Sahib is the central scripture of Sikhism, regarded by Sikhs as their final and eternal Guru. Its compilation was completed on 29 August 1604, and it was first installed in the Golden Temple at Amritsar on 1 September 1604.
k: The holy book of the Sikhs was finished in 1604 and placed in the Golden Temple at Amritsar.

s: The Basilica of Bom Jesus is a Catholic basilica in Goa, in the Konkan region, and a centre of pilgrimage.
k: The Basilica of Bom Jesus is a famous old church in Goa that pilgrims visit.

s: The Akal Takht in Amritsar is the most prominent of the five takhts, the seats of authority of the Sikhs.
k: The Akal Takht is the most important seat of authority for Sikhs. It stands beside the Golden Temple.

s: The naval Battle of Swally took place on 29–30 November 1612 off the coast of Suvali, a village near Surat, and was a victory for four English East India Company ships.
k: In 1612 four English ships won a sea battle near Surat.

s: Kota State, also known as Kotah, was a princely state in the Hadoti region of Rajasthan, dated from 1613.
k: Kota was a kingdom in Rajasthan from the 1600s.

s: Sirmur was a princely state in the region that is now the Sirmaur district of Himachal Pradesh.
k: Sirmur was a small kingdom in the Himalayan foothills.

s: Tharangambadi, formerly Tranquebar, on the Coromandel Coast of Tamil Nadu, was established on 19 November 1620 as the first Danish trading post in India.
k: In 1620 traders from Denmark set up their first trading post in India, at Tranquebar on the east coast.

s: Itmad Ud Daulah is a Mughal mausoleum in Agra, built between 1622 and 1628.
k: This Mughal tomb in Agra was finished in 1628, a few years before work began on the Taj Mahal.

s: The Pathar Mosque, known locally as Naev Masheed, is a Mughal-era stone mosque in the old city of Srinagar.
k: The Pathar Mosque is a stone mosque built in Srinagar in Mughal times.

s: Datia State, ruled by a branch of the Bundela Rajputs, was a princely state in subsidiary alliance with British India.
k: Datia was a kingdom of the Bundela Rajputs in central India.

s: The Bhangarh Fort is a 16th-century fort in Rajasthan, around which a town was established.
k: Bhangarh in Rajasthan is a fort and town from the 1500s.

t: Jahanara, first lady of the empire
s: Jahanara Begum was the eldest surviving child of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan and Mumtaz Mahal. After her mother's death in 1631, the 17-year-old Jahanara was entrusted with the royal seal and given the title Padshah Begum.
k: When the empress Mumtaz Mahal died in 1631, her 17-year-old daughter Jahanara was put in charge of the royal seal of the Mughal Empire.

s: The Mughal emperor Jahangir is buried in a mausoleum dating from 1637 in Shahdara Bagh, on the bank of the Ravi near Lahore.
k: The emperor Jahangir is buried in a tomb beside the river Ravi, near Lahore.

s: The Khanate of Kalat, also known as the Brahui Confederacy, originated in the Kalat region of today's Pakistan.
k: Kalat was a kingdom of the Brahui people in Balochistan.

s: The Gardens of Babur are a historic site in Kabul, Afghanistan.
k: The Gardens of Babur are a historic garden in Kabul.

s: Fort St. George at Chennai, founded in 1639, was the first English fortress in India. Its construction gave the impetus for further settlement and trade, and a city grew around it.
k: In 1639 English traders built a fort on the coast. The city of Chennai grew up around it.

s: The Wazir Khan Mosque is a 17th-century Mughal mosque in the city of Lahore.
k: The Wazir Khan Mosque in Lahore was built in Mughal times, almost 400 years ago.

s: The Shalamar Gardens in Lahore are a 17th-century Mughal garden complex.
k: The Shalamar Gardens in Lahore were laid out by the Mughals almost 400 years ago.

s: The Chogyals, of the Namgyal dynasty, were the monarchs of the former Kingdom of Sikkim. The Chogyal was the absolute monarch of Sikkim from 1642 to 1973.
k: From 1642 the mountain kingdom of Sikkim was ruled by kings called Chogyals.

s: The Red Fort in Old Delhi is a historic Mughal fort that served as the main residence of the Mughal emperors.
k: The Red Fort in Delhi was the home of the Mughal emperors.

s: Biryani is a mixed rice dish traditionally made with spiced meat, seafood or vegetables. It was present in Mughal-era India, though whether it was created there is debated.
k: Biryani, a dish of rice cooked with spices and meat or vegetables, was eaten in the India of the Mughal emperors. Nobody is sure where it was invented.

s: Jagdish Temple is a large Hindu temple in the middle of Udaipur in Rajasthan, just outside the royal palace. It dates from 1651.
k: The Jagdish Temple in Udaipur was built in 1651, next to the royal palace.

s: The Masjid-i-Jehan-Numa, commonly known as the Jama Masjid, in Old Delhi is one of the largest mosques in India.
k: The Jama Masjid in Delhi is one of the biggest mosques in India.

s: The Gol Gumbaz in Bijapur is a mausoleum of dark grey basalt holding the tomb of Mohammad Adil Shah, seventh ruler of the Bijapur Sultanate. Building halted in 1656, at his death.
k: The Gol Gumbaz in Bijapur is the huge domed tomb of a sultan. Work on it stopped when he died in 1656.

s: The Shah Jahan Mosque, or Friday Mosque of Thatta, is the main congregational mosque of the city of Thatta in Sindh.
k: The emperor Shah Jahan had a great mosque built in the city of Thatta in Sindh.

s: The Battle of Pratapgad took place on 10 November 1659 at Pratapgad in Satara, fought by the Maratha forces led by Shivaji.
k: On 10 November 1659 Shivaji's Maratha army fought a battle at Pratapgad.

s: The Bibi Ka Maqbara, a tomb in Aurangabad, Maharashtra, was commissioned in 1660 by Prince Azam Shah, son of the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb.
k: A Mughal prince, the son of the emperor Aurangzeb, had a tomb built at Aurangabad in 1660.

s: The Battle of Pavan Khind was a rearguard last stand in 1660 at a mountain pass in the vicinity of Vishalgad.
k: In 1660 a rearguard made a last stand in a mountain pass near Vishalgad.

s: Dutch Malabar, also known by the name of its main settlement, Cochin, was a collection of settlements and trading posts of the Dutch East India Company on the Malabar Coast between 1661 and 1795.
k: From 1661 to 1795 the Dutch trading company held Cochin and other ports on the coast of Kerala.

s: Gurdwara Bangla Sahib is one of the most prominent Sikh houses of worship in Delhi.
k: Gurdwara Bangla Sahib is a famous Sikh place of worship in Delhi.

s: The Gyanvapi Mosque is a mosque in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, dated to the 1660s.
k: The Gyanvapi Mosque in Varanasi was built in the 1660s.

s: The Battle of Purandar was fought between the Mughal Empire and the Marathas in 1665.
k: In 1665 the Mughals and the Marathas fought at the fort of Purandar.

s: The Kingdom of Mewar, later known as Udaipur State, was an independent Hindu kingdom in the Mewar region of Rajputana.
k: Mewar was a proud Rajput kingdom. Its later capital was the city of Udaipur.

s: French India was a French colony of five separated enclaves that began as trading posts of the French East India Company: Pondichéry, Karikal, Yanaon, Mahé and Chandernagor. They joined India in 1950 and 1954.
k: France ruled five small pieces of land on the coasts of India, such as Pondicherry. They became part of India in the 1950s.

s: The Battle of Sinhagad, also known as the Battle of Kondhana, was a Maratha attack on a Mughal-held fort during the night of 4 February 1670.
k: On the night of 4 February 1670 the Marathas attacked the fort of Sinhagad, which the Mughals held.

s: The Mahabat Khan Mosque is a 17th-century Mughal-era mosque, dated to 1670.
k: The Mahabat Khan Mosque was built in Mughal times, in 1670.

s: Baba Budan, a 17th-century Sufi whose shrine is at Baba Budangiri in Karnataka, is known to have first introduced the coffee plant to India. He brought seven raw beans from the port of Mokha in Yemen on his way back from the hajj in 1670.
k: In 1670 a holy man named Baba Budan came home from Arabia with seven coffee beans and planted them in the hills of Karnataka. That is how coffee came to India.

s: The Badshahi Mosque in Lahore is an imperial mosque of the Mughal era, constructed from 1671.
k: The Badshahi Mosque in Lahore was built by the Mughal emperor in the 1670s.

s: The Battle of Saraighat was a naval battle fought in 1671 between the Mughal Empire and the Ahom Kingdom on the Brahmaputra river at Saraighat, now in Guwahati, Assam.
k: In 1671 the boats of the Ahom kingdom of Assam fought the Mughal navy on the Brahmaputra river.

s: Hemis Monastery is a Himalayan Buddhist monastery of the Drukpa Lineage on the bank of the Indus in Ladakh, 45 km from Leh. It was re-established in 1672.
k: Hemis is a Buddhist monastery beside the Indus River in the high mountains of Ladakh.

s: The Maratha Empire, or Maratha Confederacy, was an early modern polity in the Indian subcontinent, dated from Shivaji's coronation in 1674.
k: Shivaji was crowned king of the Marathas in 1674. His kingdom grew into an empire.

s: The Thanjavur Maratha kingdom, ruled by the Bhonsle dynasty, was a South Indian monarchy dated from 1674.
k: From 1674 a Maratha family ruled the old city of Thanjavur in the Tamil country.

s: The Tibet–Ladakh–Mughal war of 1679–1684 was fought between the central Tibetan government and Ladakh, with the Mughal Empire involved.
k: From 1679 to 1684 Tibet and Ladakh fought a war in the high Himalaya.

s: Tawang Monastery in Arunachal Pradesh is the largest Buddhist monastery in India. It was founded by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso in 1680–1681, in accordance with the wishes of the 5th Dalai Lama.
k: The biggest Buddhist monastery in India is at Tawang, in the mountains of Arunachal Pradesh. It was founded in 1680.

s: Bharatpur was a tributary of the House of Scindia and later a princely state under British suzerainty.
k: Bharatpur was a princely state.

s: The Battle of Itakhuli was fought in August 1682 between the Ahom Kingdom and the Mughal Empire, in modern-day Assam.
k: In 1682 the Ahom kingdom of Assam fought the Mughals at Itakhuli.

s: The Anglo-Mughal war of 1686–1690, also known as Child's War, was the first Anglo-Indian war on the Indian subcontinent.
k: From 1686 to 1690 the English East India Company fought its first war in India, against the Mughal Empire.

s: The State of Bahawalpur was a state in the Punjab region that existed as a sovereign polity from 1748 to 1833 and later as a princely state.
k: Bahawalpur was a state in the Punjab region.

s: The siege of Jinji, 1690–1698, was a protracted conflict between the Mughal Empire and the Maratha kingdom over a triple-hill fortress.
k: The Mughals besieged the Maratha hill fortress of Jinji for eight years.

s: The Battle of Nadaun in 1691 was fought at Nadaun between Raja Bhim Chand of Bilaspur and the Mughals.
k: In 1691 the hill king of Bilaspur fought the Mughals at Nadaun.

s: Paro Taktsang is a sacred Buddhist site on the cliffside of the upper Paro valley in Bhutan, one of the Tiger's Nest caves linked to Padmasambhava. The monastery complex was built in 1692.
k: Paro Taktsang, the Tiger's Nest, is a Buddhist monastery built on a cliff in Bhutan in 1692.

s: Mecca Masjid in Hyderabad, Telangana, is one of the largest mosques in India.
k: The Mecca Masjid in Hyderabad is one of the largest mosques in India.

s: Fort William in Calcutta was built during the early years of British administration in Bengal.
k: The British built Fort William at Calcutta in their early years in Bengal.

t: Kanhoji Angre, admiral of the Marathas
s: Kanhoji Angre, who died on 4 July 1729, was an admiral of the Maratha Navy, known for attacking and capturing European merchant ships and collecting tolls from them, despite the efforts of the Portuguese and British to stop him.
k: Kanhoji Angre was the admiral of the Maratha navy. He captured the ships of European traders, and they could not stop him.

s: The Khalsa is both the community that follows Sikhism and a special group of initiated Sikhs. The tradition was initiated in 1699 by the tenth Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, and its founding is celebrated at the festival of Vaisakhi.
k: In 1699 the tenth Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, created the Khalsa, a community of initiated Sikhs. Sikhs celebrate this every year at Vaisakhi.

s: Maharani Tarabai Bhonsle, daughter-in-law of Shivaji, was regent of the Maratha Empire from 1700 until 1708.
k: From 1700 to 1708 the Marathas were led by a queen, Tarabai.

s: The Calico Acts of 1700 and 1721 were acts of the English and British parliaments that banned the import of most cotton textiles into England and then restricted their sale. They were a precursor to the Industrial Revolution, when Britain surpassed India as the world's leading textile manufacturer.
k: India once made more cloth than any other country. England passed laws to keep Indian cotton cloth out, and later began making cloth in its own factories.

s: The Battle of Anandpur in 1700 was fought at Anandpur between the armies of the Sikh Guru Gobind Singh and Mughal forces.
k: In 1700 the army of Guru Gobind Singh fought the Mughals at Anandpur.

s: Kolhapur State was a Maratha princely state in the Deccan, dated from 1707.
k: Kolhapur was a Maratha kingdom in the Deccan.

s: The Hotak Empire was an Afghan dynasty founded by Ghilji Pashtuns, dated from 1709.
k: In 1709 the Hotak family founded an Afghan kingdom.

s: The Battle of Chappar Chiri, also called the Battle of Sirhind, was fought between the Mughal Empire and the Sikhs on 12 May 1710.
k: On 12 May 1710 the Sikhs fought the Mughals at Chappar Chiri.

s: Baroda State was a kingdom within the Maratha Empire and later a princely state of the British Indian Empire.
k: Baroda was a Maratha kingdom in Gujarat. Later it became one of India's biggest princely states.

s: Hyderabad State, also called the Nizamate of Hyderabad, was a princely state in the Deccan region of south-central India.
k: Hyderabad was a large kingdom in the Deccan, ruled by a prince called the Nizam.

s: Jaipur, the capital and largest city of Rajasthan, was founded in 1727.
k: The city of Jaipur was founded in 1727 by King Sawai Jai Singh.

s: The Kingdom of Travancore, also known as Thiruvithamkoor, was a state at the southern tip of India, later a princely state.
k: Travancore was a kingdom in the far south of India, in what is now Kerala.

s: In September 1730, 363 Bishnois were killed while trying peacefully to protect a grove of khejri trees from being cut down on the orders of the Maharaja of Marwar.
k: In 1730 villagers called Bishnois tried peacefully to stop a king's men from cutting down their trees. 363 of them were killed.

s: The City Palace in Jaipur is a royal residence and the former administrative headquarters of the rulers of Jaipur, dated to 1732.
k: The City Palace in Jaipur was the home of the kings of Jaipur.

s: Indore State was a kingdom within the Maratha Empire, ruled by the Maratha Holkar dynasty.
k: Indore was the kingdom of the Holkar family, part of the Maratha Empire.

s: The Battle of Karnal in 1739 was a decisive victory for Nader Shah, founder of the Afsharid dynasty of Iran.
k: In 1739 Nader Shah, the ruler of Iran, won a great victory at Karnal in northern India.

s: The Travancore–Dutch War, 1739–1753, was a war between the Dutch East India Company and the Indian kingdom of Travancore.
k: The kingdom of Travancore fought a war against the Dutch trading company.

s: The Battle of Colachel was fought on 10 August 1741 between the Indian kingdom of Travancore and the Dutch East India Company.
k: On 10 August 1741 the army of Travancore fought the Dutch at Colachel.

s: The Carnatic wars were a series of military conflicts in the middle of the 18th century in India's coastal Carnatic region.
k: In the 1700s the British and French trading companies fought each other in southern India.

s: The First Carnatic War, 1746–1748, was the Indian theatre of the War of the Austrian Succession and the first of the Carnatic wars.
k: In the 1740s a big war in Europe, the War of the Austrian Succession, was also fought in India. It was the first of the wars that made the British strong on India's east coast.

s: The Battle of Madras took place in September 1746, during the War of the Austrian Succession, when a French force attacked the British-held town.
k: In 1746 the French attacked Madras, which the British held.

s: The Durrani Empire, colloquially known as the Kingdom of Afghanistan or the Afghan Empire, dates from 1747.
k: The Durrani Empire, founded in 1747, is also known as the Afghan Empire.

s: The Sikh Confederacy was a confederation of twelve sovereign Sikh states that rose during the 18th century.
